purpose: silver_nyc_planes is the cleaned aircraft reference table for the NYC flights domain: one row per registered tail number, carrying airframe type, manufacturer, model, engine configuration, seat count, cruise speed, and manufacture year. It feeds joins from flight-level fact tables that key on tailnum, and supports fleet-composition and aircraft-age analysis.
usage: Join to flight data on tailnum, which is the declared grain and is non-null for all 3322 rows. Treat speed as optional context only: it is populated for 23 rows out of 3322, so any average or filter on it must be written against the populated subset deliberately. Use is_rotorcraft to exclude helicopters when analysis assumes fixed-wing commercial service. Manufacturer strings are registry spellings and are not canonicalized, so group with care.
limitations: No deduplication was applied because duplicate_row_rate is 0.0, so any future duplicate tailnum rows would surface as a grain violation rather than being silently collapsed. speed is effectively unusable for aggregate analysis at a 0.993076 null rate, and year is missing for 70 rows (0.021072). Manufacturer variants such as 'AIRBUS' versus 'AIRBUS INDUSTRIE' remain unresolved, and model is kept as text because its values mix digits, letters, and punctuation. The dropped Airbyte metadata columns mean this table carries no load lineage; lineage must be recovered from the bronze layer.
